source.title: Reviewing an Engineering Apprenticeship Programme
source.author: Dual Dictionary project — AI-assisted original source
source.article: An engineering firm is updating its apprenticeship programme to help trainees move through design, testing, and customer-support teams. Each apprentice begins with two weeks of safety training, then takes on supervised tasks that match their current skills. Mentors set out a goal for every rotation and meet trainees at the midpoint to review progress. If a trainee has already mastered a task, the mentor arranges a more demanding assignment instead of repeating the same exercise. Supervisors compare written feedback with practical assessments before agreeing on the next placement. Trainees are encouraged to work towards a professional certificate, while managers track whether the rotations provide enough experience in every department. The programme lead will follow up with mentors after each cycle and adjust the schedule where necessary.

exercises.prompt: In sentence s2, what does 'takes on' mean when the apprentice 'takes on supervised tasks that match their current skills'?

options.text: It means the apprentice accepts and starts doing supervised tasks that fit their skills.
options.explanation: This is correct because it matches the meaning of accepting and starting a responsibility.

options.text: It means the apprentice gives the supervised tasks to another trainee to do.
options.explanation: This is wrong because giving tasks to someone else is the opposite of accepting them.

options.text: It means the apprentice only watches the supervised tasks without doing them.
options.explanation: This is wrong because watching without doing does not involve accepting responsibility.

options.text: It means the apprentice delays the supervised tasks until a later time.
options.explanation: This is wrong because delaying tasks does not mean starting them now.

exercises.explanation: Only option a correctly paraphrases takes on as accepting and starting tasks in s2.

exercises.prompt: Choose the sentence that uses 'takes on' naturally and correctly.

options.text: After her safety training, she takes on challenging projects in the design team.
options.explanation: This is correct because the verb form and collocation takes on + object are natural.

options.text: After her safety training, she take on challenging projects in the design team.
options.explanation: This is wrong because take should be corrected to takes to agree with she.

options.text: After her safety training, she takes on to lead challenging projects in the design team.
options.explanation: This is wrong because to lead should be corrected to leading after takes on.

options.text: After her safety training, she takes on with challenging projects in the design team.
options.explanation: This is wrong because the extra preposition with should be removed after takes on.

exercises.explanation: Only option a uses takes on with correct grammar and collocation.

exercises.prompt: In sentence s6, what does 'work towards' mean when trainees are 'encouraged to work towards a professional certificate'?

options.text: It means the trainees make steady efforts over time to earn a professional certificate.
options.explanation: This is correct because it describes gradual effort to achieve a goal.

options.text: It means the trainees receive a professional certificate immediately without effort.
options.explanation: This is wrong because immediate receipt without effort ignores steady progress.

options.text: It means the trainees avoid trying to earn a professional certificate.
options.explanation: This is wrong because avoiding a goal is the opposite of working toward it.

options.text: It means the trainees give up their attempt to earn a professional certificate.
options.explanation: This is wrong because giving up means stopping effort, not continuing it.

exercises.explanation: Only option a correctly paraphrases work towards as steady effort to achieve a goal.

exercises.prompt: Choose the sentence that uses 'working towards' naturally and correctly.

options.text: Our team is working towards launching the new product by December.
options.explanation: This is correct because working towards is correctly followed by the gerund launching.

options.text: Our team is working towards launch the new product by December.
options.explanation: This is wrong because launch should be corrected to launching after towards.

options.text: Our team is work towards launching the new product by December.
options.explanation: This is wrong because work should be corrected to working after is.

options.text: Our team is working towards for launching the new product by December.
options.explanation: This is wrong because the extra preposition for should be removed after towards.

exercises.explanation: Only option a uses working towards with correct grammar and collocation.

exercises.prompt: You are writing a short personal message to a friend about your fitness goal. Write 2-3 sentences describing your steady efforts and use the phrase work towards naturally.
exercises.sampleAnswer: I have started running every morning before work. I am working towards completing my first half-marathon in spring.
selfCheck: I wrote 2-3 sentences as a personal message to a friend about a fitness goal.
I described steady efforts and used working towards naturally with correct grammar.
My message is clear, natural, and different from the workplace training context.
